Title: Tesla Is Burning Through Top Employees - Why Are They All Leaving?

Summary: 
Elon Musk's leadership style at Tesla has been described as mercurial and has led to a significant exodus of top employees in 2025, particularly affecting key departments including US sales, battery and power-train operations, public affairs, the chief information officer role, and core teams behind the Optimus robot and artificial intelligence initiatives. Notable departures include Troy Jones, VP of sales, service, and delivery for North America, who left after over a decade; Omead Afshar, chief of sales and manufacturing and described as 'Musk's fixer' and one of Tesla’s most powerful executives; Jenna Ferrua, head of human resources; and Milan Kovac, engineering executive overseeing the Optimus project. According to Andrej Karpathy, former AI director at Tesla and a founding member of OpenAI, Musk favors small, highly technical teams and routinely pushes for removing low performers, even when others advocate for retention. This pattern of downsizing began with Musk’s acquisition of X (formerly Twitter) in 2022, where the workforce was reduced by 80% between 2021 and 2025, shrinking to nearly 1,500 employees. Power struggles led to the resignation of former X CEO Linda Yaccarino, who stepped down after the company merged with xAI. These events highlight a broader trend of executive turnover and organizational instability under Musk’s leadership across his companies, including Tesla, SpaceX, the Boring Company, X, and xAI.

Title: Musk prévient que Tesla, en recul au 2e trimestre, pourrait avoir un passage à vide

Summary: 
Tesla's CEO Elon Musk has warned that the company may experience 'a few difficult quarters' by the end of 2026 due to the loss of advantages related to the transition to electric vehicles and waiting for the large-scale deployment of autonomous driving. 'We are in a strange phase of transition where we will lose many advantages in the US (...) and where we are at the beginning of autonomy,' Musk said during an audio conference. He added that the company could experience some difficult quarters, including the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first and second quarters of 2026. However, Musk assured that once autonomy is 'deployed on a large scale in the second half of 2026, the situation will improve.' Tesla is currently facing a crucial turning point related to autonomous driving and artificial intelligence. The company has mentioned an 'acceleration over time of revenues generated by AI, software, and fleets.' According to Wedbush analysts, autonomy alone represents around $1,000 billion in valuation for the company. Tesla has already launched a robotaxi service in Austin and plans to expand it to San Francisco and other locations. Musk stated that 'if we obtain the necessary regulatory approvals, we could cover half of the US population by the end of the year.' In the meantime, the company will focus on recovering its global vehicle sales, which have declined by 13.5% over the past year. The decline is attributed to a lack of renewal of its product lineup, increased competition in China, Elon Musk's involvement in US politics, and a slowdown in the electric vehicle market. The removal of the $7,500 tax credit in the US, scheduled for September 30, is expected to boost sales in the short term but then slow them down, according to experts.

Title: Tesla-Organigramm: Diese Manager leiten das Unternehmen von Elon Musk

Summary: 
Despite ongoing turbulence, Elon Musk has retained several long-standing executives in key leadership roles at Tesla. According to an internal organizational chart reviewed by Business Insider (BI), Musk, listed as 'CEO and Technoking,' had 19 direct reports in August 2024—down from 35 in 2024 and 30 at the end of 2021. Over the past three years, he has kept nine of his direct subordinates, including Franz von Holzhausen (Design Chief, since 2008), Ashok Elluswamy (Vice President of AI Software), Lars Moravy (Vice President of Vehicle Engineering), and Tom Zhu (Senior Vice President of Manufacturing in China). Internal salary data from 2024 reveals significant leadership turnover: at least three HR heads and multiple senior lawyers have been replaced since 2021, and approximately two-thirds of Musk’s direct reports have left between December 2021 and September 2025. Notable departures include Troy Jones (former North American Sales Chief, over 15 years at Tesla), Omead Afshar (‘Musk Whisperer’), and Milan Kovac (leader of the humanoid robot team), who left in June 2024. Other key exits include CIO Nagesh Saldi and Daniel Ho, who moved to Waymo. Most of Musk’s direct reports are based in San Francisco, as confirmed by LinkedIn data. Musk has no direct reports in HR following Jenna Ferrua’s departure in June 2024. Leadership changes occurred in two waves: April–August 2025 and October 2024, ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi Event. The departures coincided with a challenging period for Tesla, marked by declining vehicle deliveries and reduced EV subsidies under the Trump administration. The company also faced scrutiny over Musk’s succession plan, tied to a proposed compensation package requiring him to appoint a successor, achieve a $8.5 billion market cap (approx. €7.2 billion), and deploy one million autonomous vehicles.

Published date: September 30 2025, 14:47

URL: https://www.businessinsider.de/wirtschaft/tesla-organigramm-diese-manager-leiten-das-unternehmen-von-elon-musk/
Source: Business Insider
Classification: Business
Sentiment: neutral
Reporting voice: Analytical
Continent: North America

Title: Tesla Executive In Charge Of Supercomputer Project Resigns

Summary: 
Peter Bannon, Tesla's executive in charge of the Dojo supercomputer project, has resigned after nearly 10 years with the company. According to reports, CEO Elon Musk has ordered Bannon's team to shut down, with engineers reassigned to other projects. Musk has been trying to pivot Tesla into an artificial intelligence and robotics company, with Dojo being a key part of this transformation. The supercomputer was designed to process and train AI models, improve driver assistance systems, and help turn Tesla vehicles into self-driving robotaxis. Musk had previously stated that the newest version of Dojo would be 'operating at scale sometime next year.' This news comes as Tesla experiences an exodus of top talent, with the company struggling with declining electric vehicle sales and a sinking share price. TSLA stock has fallen 15% in 2025, trading at $322.27 per share.
